title: AI Agents for Enabling Autonomous Experiments at ORNL's HPC and Manufacturing User Facilities
problem: Scientific experimentation across heterogeneous HPC and manufacturing facilities requires manual coordination, limiting throughput and hindering rapid iteration. Lack of automation prevents tight coupling between experimental and computational workflows.
motivation: Research institutions operate multiple user facilities (HPC, manufacturing) with different interfaces and capabilities. Automating cross-facility orchestration reduces coordination overhead, accelerates discovery, and enables closed-loop optimization.
method: The system uses a team of AI agents (software that makes autonomous decisions) to coordinate experiments by translating plain English descriptions into instructions via an AI language model. These agents communicate with equipment and supercomputers through standard software interfaces (APIs), while maintaining a complete workflow record so results can be reproduced and understood. The approach was tested on additive manufacturing (3D printing) experiments requiring real-time coordination with supercomputers.
key_novelty: AI agents automatically coordinate between supercomputers and manufacturing equipment, making adjustments based on real-time feedback instead of waiting for manual decisions.
contributions: Modular AI-agent architecture for cross-facility orchestration
Natural language interface enabling researcher interaction
Programmable facility APIs for heterogeneous systems
Reduced coordination overhead and accelerated discovery cycles
workloads: Additive manufacturing experiments with HPC simulation
limitations: Evaluation limited to simulated manufacturing facility; real deployment results not presented. Generalization to other scientific domains unclear. LLM hallucination and error recovery not addressed. Scalability to many concurrent experiments not evaluated.
